title: The Current and YoungArts announce new collaboration for artist residency program in Vermont
summary: The Current , a center for contemporary art with a mission to inspire civic engagement and broaden our understanding of the world through contemporary art, and YoungArts , a national organization that champions artists throughout their lifetimes and across all art forms, announce the launch of a new collaborative artist residency program in Vermont, supporting a YoungArts artist with a two-week residency. Interdisciplinary artist Timothy Hyunsoo Lee is currently in residence at The Current, marking the program's inaugural edition. The program marks a new partnership for YoungArts in Vermont, expanding its nationwide network of cultural partners that provide artists with opportunities to develop their practices and sustain their careers. title: Pop Art pioneer Allen Jones explores performance and figure in new London exhibition
summary: Gazelli Art House is presenting In Town Tonight, the first solo exhibition by Allen Jones RA (b. 1937, Southampton) with the gallery. Bringing together a substantial body of new work made between 2024 and 2026 with significant works from across his career, the exhibition presents Jones as an artist whose investigation of the human figure, performance, and the relationship between image and object remains in active evolution. A defining figure of British Pop Art, Jones emerged at the forefront of a generation that transformed British visual culture in the early 1960s. Across more than six decades, his distinctive and often provocative approach to the human figure-in painting, sculpture, printmaking and photography-has continually challenged conventional distinctions between surface and form, image and object. At the heart of In Town Tonight is a new series of shaped canvas paintings that brings the theatricality of performance into Jones's latest work. A palette of intense green, yellow

title: Kunsthistorisches Museum investigates Cleopatra's family intrigue in 'Crime Scene Ephesus'
summary: Ephesus, one of the most important cities of the ancient world, serves as the murder scene of Cleopatra’s sister Arsinoë IV in 41 BCE. Who ordered her assassination? And what role did the political upheavals of the time play in her death? These questions are explored in the culture-historical exhibition Crime Scene Ephesus. Cleopatra and Rome. More than 100 objects tell the story of the most powerful figures of the time: the last queen of Egypt, her allies, and lovers – Caesar and Marc Antony, as well as her adversary Augustus – and of the ancient metropolises of Rome, Alexandria, and Ephesus as centres of power, art, knowledge, and political intrigue. The exhibition takes us to the magnificent city of Ephesus, the setting for a 2,000-year-old crime story and the site of a monumental funerary structure: the so-called Octagon. title: Almine Rech Paris presents Robert Indiana's first solo exhibition with the gallery
summary: Almine Rech Paris is presenting Robert Indiana's first monographic exhibition with the gallery, organized in collaboration with The Robert Indiana Legacy Initiative, on view from October 17, 2026 to January 23, 2027. Concurrent with the exhibition, a monumental LOVE sculpture (LOVE WALL, 1966 - 2006) by the artist will be on view as part of Art Basel Paris' public program. "The technique, if successful, is that happy transmutation of the lost into the found, junk into art, the neglected into the wanted, the unloved into the loved, dross into gold, hence: alchemy." — Robert Indiana, 1961¹ Robert Indiana’s work is rooted in acts of transformation. title: Pulitzer Arts Foundation presents Olga de Amaral: Weaving the Infinite
summary: The Pulitzer Arts Foundation announces the recent opening of a major retrospective dedicated to Colombian fiber artist Olga de Amaral (b. 1932), co-organized with Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. Amaral is known internationally for her virtuosic textile works, which blur the boundaries between weaving, sculpture, and painting. On view at the Pulitzer through January 31, 2027, and at Cooper Hewitt beginning in April 2027, Olga de Amaral: Weaving the Infinite is co-curated by Stephanie Weissberg, Senior Curator at the Pulitzer, and Christina L. De León, Associate Curator of Latino Design at Cooper Hewitt. Featuring textiles and works on paper created over more than 60 years, Olga de Amaral: Weaving the Infinite is the most comprehensive examination to date of the artist’s foundational contributions to the fiber arts movement and design. title: Perrotin presents new bronze sculptures and wall reliefs by Alma Allen
summary: When a collector once asked Jean-Michel Basquiat for his C.V., the artist offered to draw around the outline of his hand. I imagine Alma Allen’s hands, too, as a record of his experience: whorled and rubbed, smoothed and shattered — ‘plump with struggle’, as one critic described Allen’s life story. Though his sculptures take their final form in the hard stuff of stone, wood and, more recently, metal, each one still begins, as they have since he began carving with a pocketknife as a teenager in Utah, in the immediacy of the hand: the artist working pieces of string, clay or wax through his fingers, pushing their limits, finding the point where they have poise and weight. It’s a meditative practice, the aim is not mastery over these materials, nor to realise some predetermined intention through them, but to release a potential form that is somehow already there. ‘To have my hands teach me something’, is how Allen puts it. title: Christie's presents masterworks from a French-American collection
summary: Christie's announced Anthology of Design: Masterworks from a French-American Collection, an extraordinary single-owner sale of design taking place on December 9th at Christie's New York. This visionary collection was assembled over the course of more than twenty years, built by a transatlantic collector with a formidable eye. Forward-thinking in his approach, the collector was ahead of his time, acquiring the best names before they were as highly coveted as they have now come to be. The collection consists of more than 100 objects that are defined by their rarity, integrity of form, and exceptional provenance. There are offerings of signature pieces from all leading icons in the field, bringing together the whimsy of François-Xavier Lalanne, the discipline of Jean Prouvé, the geometry of Charlotte Perriand, the material freedom of Ron Arad, the architectural invention of Ettore Sottsass and the sculptural prowess of the Giacomettis. title: National Gallery and Arts Council England announce nationwide touring exhibition 'Collected'
summary: The first exhibition of objects and works of art acquired for the nation through the Acceptance in Lieu and Cultural Gifts schemes will open at the National Gallery next spring (22 May – 5 September 2027) before a nationwide tour. The schemes are delivered by Arts Council England on behalf of the UK Government and for the benefit of the four home nations. Collected showcases a range of important artistic and cultural objects – centuries of art, saved and shared –transferred from private collections to public collections through both schemes, demonstrating their impact across the country. Over many decades, these schemes have ensured thousands of objects have been allocated, free of charge, to public museums, galleries, libraries and archives across the UK. Visitors will explore the journeys that brought these diverse, inspiring and significant works from private hands into public care and the collaborative partnerships that help preserve our shared cultural heritage. title: Kunstmuseum Bern unveils 2027 season led by Franz Marc and Camille Bombois retrospectives
summary: Existentially charged depictions of animals, life in heightened reality, and digital worlds: in 2027, the Kunstmuseum Bern invites visitors to immerse themselves in pictorial universes of remarkable diversity. The exhibition year opens with the first comprehensive presentation in Switzerland of the vibrant paintings of Franz Marc, which are among the most famous works of modern art. With [ENTER HERE]. Digital Worlds, the museum presents its first exhibition dedicated to immersive digital art. The highlight in the autumn is the first major presentation of the French artist Camille Bombois in Switzerland. The programme is complemented by three thematic focuses drawn from the collection. A blue horse, a yellow cow, a purple fox: the vibrant colours of Franz Marc’s (1880–1916) animal paintings are captivating to this day. title: Ferrari Daytona SP3 heads incredible twenty-two strong Ferrari line-up at RM Sotheby's London sale
summary: The 2022 Daytona SP3 makes a compelling case to be considered the most desirable Ferrari of the 21st century. After paying tribute to its open-top sportscars of the late 1940s and 1950s with the Monza SP1 and SP2, Ferrari used its third ‘Icona’ creation to honour its mid-engined prototypes of the 1960s. Unveiled in 2022, the Daytona SP3 is considered by many to be the most beautiful Ferrari of the modern era. The Daytona SP3 employs a 6.5-litre, 65-degree V-12 the engine, boasting 829 bhp and is the most potent non-electrically assisted 12-cylinder engine in Ferrari road car history. title: Esther Schipper presents Philippe Parreno's atmospheric installations in Paris
summary: Esther Schipper presents a selection of works by Philippe Parreno at its Paris gallery on Place Vendôme. Transformed into a domestic interior, the gallery’s apartment-like setting becomes a changing environment in which architecture, objects, and natural light participate in a choreography unfolding over time. Occupying the central room is Membrane, a cluster of antennae sensing and collecting atmospheric data, including temperature, pressure, humidity, and breath, orchestrating movement and light throughout the space. Two motorized blinds move independently across the windows. Alternately veiling and revealing the openings, like a pair of eyes opening and closing, they modulate the room’s luminosity and, with it, the appearance of everything it contains. These shifting conditions activate Chronochromes (2026), a wallpaper in which a palm motif repeats across a phosphorescent surface. title: Pace to present solo booth of Emily Kam Kngwarray at inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi
summary: Pace will present a solo booth of paintings by Emily Kam Kngwarray, one of Australia’s most celebrated artists, at the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi. The presentation will include a selection of never-before-exhibited paintings alongside works that featured in the gallery’s recent exhibition Emily Kam Kngwarray: The Turning Season held in New York. The works on view span the artist’s entire career, from her early batik textiles and paintings through to her later colorist canvases and abstractions inspired by the anwerlarr yam. A member of the Anmatyerr people of Alhalker in Australia’s Northern Territory, Kngwarray grounded her practice in Indigenous Australian knowledge systems and a profound custodial connection to ancestral lands. summary: Christie's announces the Hong Kong Magnificent Jewels Autumn Live Auction on 24 November 2026 during Hong Kong Luxury Week, bringing together more than 120 exceptional jewels. title: Four artists dismantle Western power and mythologies in new Harvard exhibition
summary: Knowledge Is Myth: Chimeric Continuities features works by four artists and collectives Enzo Camacho & Ami Lien, Candice Lin, Cole Lu, and Ayoung Yu & Nicholas Oh that complicate the binaries of mythology and knowledge, and their constructs. The title Knowledge Is Myth plays off the phrase “knowledge is power,” popularized by Sir Francis Bacon in the late sixteenth century at the height of the European Enlightenment, globalization, and religious conflict. Drawing from diasporic as well as chimeric and hybrid subjectivities, these works reconfigure colonial hierarchies of being that separate human and nonhuman realms, while embracing what decolonial writers Walter Mignolo and Catherine E. Walsh describe as an ecology of knowledge informed by non-Western epistemologies,² carried through myths and the power of storytelling.³

title: Institut suédois dedicates autumn exhibition to contemporary master Andreas Eriksson
summary: The Institut suédois is dedicating its autumn exhibition to Andreas Eriksson (b. 1975), a leading figure in the contemporary art scene. His meditative work, with its rich verdant tones, is interspersed with that of Ivan Aguéli (1869–1917), artist, thinker and seasoned traveller. Applying paint in blocks, layers and brushstrokes, Andreas Eriksson builds visual structures that can be interpreted as ways of experiencing the world. Geological strata, minerals, moss, leaves and bark: his paintings are layers of materiality, accumulations of energy and time in a variety of densities and forms. His art is fundamentally linked to a single place: Medelplana, at the foot of the Kinnekulle plateau, in the southwest of Sweden, near Lake Vänern. title: Hélia Paukner appointed Artistic Director of the Lyon Biennale Contemporary Art
summary: La Biennale de Lyon announces the appointment of Hélia Paukner as Artistic Director of the Contemporary Art Biennale. She succeeds Isabelle Bertolotti, who has held the position since 2018. Hélia Paukner will also become Director of macLYON – Lyon’s Museum of Contemporary Art, continuing the longstanding relationship between the two institutions. This dual appointment marks a new chapter for the Lyon Contemporary Art Biennale, a major event on the international art scene that has championed contemporary artistic creation in France and abroad for nearly forty years. Selected following a recruitment process led by the City of Lyon, in partnership with the French Ministry of Culture, the Métropole de Lyon and La Biennale de Lyon, Hélia Paukner will take up her roles on 1 February 2027. title: Serpentine unveils 2027 season featuring Pierre Alechinsky, Adrian Piper, and Matt Copson
summary: In 2027, Serpentine will unveil a series of landmark solo exhibitions bringing together artists across generations whose practices expand the possibilities of media and explore new forms of expressions. Through these ambitious shows and public art presentations, Serpentine will nurture connections between artists and audiences, continuing its unique mission of bringing art into everyday life from its unique setting within The Royal Parks. From February to April 2027, Serpentine will present a solo exhibition of Pierre Alechinsky (b.1927, Brussels, Belgium; lives and works in Bougival, France), the last surviving member of the short-lived but hugely influential European avant-garde movement, Cobra. title: Group exhibition at Palais de Tokyo highlights collective practices across regional France
summary: The exhibition brings together individual and collective artistic practices which, while situated in a range of territories – the countryside, the mountains, islands – are all rooted in a choice to work beyond urban centres. The exhibition’s title, which is borrowed from a work by Gina Proenza (“Toi et ta bande”), points to the many groups whose work is gathered here: artist collectives, high school students, choirs, communities for life, work and activism – a host of forms that reflect upon different ways of being together. The three dozen works presented in the exhibition, many of which have been produced for the occasion, have all taken shape in unique territories, including Brittany, the Cévennes, Corsica, Guadeloupe, the Hautes-Pyrénées, Limousin and the Basque Country. title: Fondation Louis Vuitton and The Broad partner for landmark 2027 Paris exhibition
summary: From April 21 to August 30, 2027, the Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris, in partnership with The Broad, Los Angeles, will present the most extensive exhibition of the Broad collection ever mounted outside Los Angeles, filling the Fondation’s Frank Gehry-designed building with 164 works. As The Broad completes construction of its museum expansion that will open in 2028, the two institutions have come together to present the collection in Paris. The exhibition will offer audiences a rare opportunity to see how Eli and Edythe Broad built one of the world’s leading collections of postwar and contemporary art, with a particular focus on US artists. They developed deep holdings of artists engaged with the subjects of their time. Their model continues to be applied today as the collection grows, adding new generations of artists. title: A forgotten 17th-century tapestry begins its journey back into the spotlight in Florence
summary: For nearly a century, a magnificent tapestry depicting the mythological story of Cupid and Psyche has remained out of sight, carefully stored away in the collections of Florence's Museo Nazionale del Bargello. Now, after decades of obscurity, the 17th-century work is beginning a long journey toward rediscovery. On October 19, The Banquet of Psyche, a monumental tapestry woven from wool and silk, left the museum for the first time in preparation for an extensive restoration. Its destination was not far away: the specialized conservation laboratory of the Opificio delle Pietre Dure, housed in the historic Palazzo Vecchio. But moving an artwork measuring 4.20 by 3.25 meters is no ordinary undertaking. title: Whitney Museum launches Jazsalyn's 'Warpmode, This is not a game!' on artport
summary: The Whitney Museum of American Art launches Warpmode, This is not a game!, a digital art project by Jazsalyn commissioned for artport, the Museum’s online gallery space for Internet art. A digital extension of the artist’s worldbuilding toolkit Warpmode, the project invites viewers to contemplate multidimensional layers of Blackness through a series of prompts. Jazsalyn produced Warpmode with the experimental curatorial project Black Beyond and published the toolkit through Metalabel in 2024. Expanding on the original physical toolkit, Warpmode, This is not a game! introduces Ancestral Intelligence as a framework for an alternative form of artificial intelligence, one rooted in the human experience of learning and developing skills and rituals. title: Sotheby's New York to offer $9 million single-owner Patek Philippe collection
summary: For many collectors, the story behind a watch is as compelling as the craftsmanship within it. Beyond mechanical ingenuity, rarity or aesthetic distinction, a timepiece carries the history of its ownership – a connection to the person who first acquired it, the life it accompanied, and the story it carries into the future. Provenance lends a watch an additional dimension of meaning, enriching its appeal with a human narrative that transcends its material value. In this respect, original ownership represents something particularly rare in the world of collecting – a direct, unbroken link to a timepiece’s beginnings. One purchase, one owner, one story. This December, Sotheby’s will present The Original Owner Collection, an exceptional group of thirty watches, nearly all of which were retained by its original owner since purchase. title: Apollo 17 astronaut's Moon-worn checklist could fetch US $400,000+ at auction
summary: A checklist worn by the last man to walk on the Moon could fetch more than US $400,000 when it goes under the hammer. The Apollo 17 checklist was strapped to astronaut Gene Cernan’s wrist during the longest single moonwalk of NASA’s Apollo programme in December 1972. The historic item, which still bears traces of lunar dust, carries an auction estimate of US $400,000+ and is being offered in a sale closing on October 22. Cernan wore the small spiral-bound booklet on his left wrist as he explored the lunar surface alongside fellow astronaut Harrison Schmitt during the mission’s second moonwalk. The pair spent seven hours, 37 minutes and 22 seconds outside their lunar module, Challenger, travelling approximately 12 miles (19.5km) in their lunar rover.
